methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $14M total raised proxy.

data.narrative:
The ePlane Company is a Series B-stage transportation venture founded by Satya Chakravarthy, currently seeking to raise $40–50M on an undisclosed valuation. The relevant comp universe consists of seven private transportation firms including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, and DeepDive; no public comparables exist in this narrow segment.

Valuation analysis relies on a single applicable method due to data constraints. Stage-progression triangulation uses the company's $14M total capital raised as a proxy base and applies a 1.9x multiplier typical of Series B-to-subsequent-stage step-ups, yielding $27M. The peer-median approach is inapplicable: while three same-sector peers exist in transportation, none qualify as true comparables when filtered by stage, adjacent-stage proximity, or similar valuation tier. Applying an all-sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given the heterogeneity of transportation subsectors.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $23M (low) to $31M (median $27M), anchored entirely on stage-progression dynamics. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-set peer valuation data, which limits cross-check capability, and the reliance on a single empirical method. The implied $40–50M fundraise would represent a 1.5x to 1.8x markup from the median estimate, a modest premium consistent with Series B momentum and funding environment conditions. Validation would require access to same-stage, same-vertical comparables or disclosure of ePlane's unit economics and technology readiness metrics.
